why: Cannot be represented inside the five-row cap without misleading. The scheme gives two mutually exclusive reason pools — E = good milk production / prolific / easy lambing / good mothers / hardy or good survival rate / good growth rate / calm or easy to handle / maternal sire, and F = hardy or good survival rate / prolific / good mothers / good growth rate / excellent conformation — nine distinct creditable points, against MAX_ROWS = 5 (types/markBank.ts:270, asserted at test/markBankDeck.test.ts:146). The tariff is 3+1, i.e. exactly two reasons, so under-representation bites immediately. The corpus's two established workarounds each fix only half of it: naming the unshown route in the r-1 contextNote (its precedent for mutually exclusive routes) still leaves the E pool's eight points needing five rows, and folding the overflow into a neighbouring row's accepts (its precedent for oversized pools) is only defensible for true synonyms — here the only genuine synonym pair is 'good mothers' / 'maternal sire', so at least two of 'easy lambing', 'good growth rate' and 'calm or easy to handle' would have to be folded under an unrelated trait. That is exactly the defect the skeptic named: a student whose two reasons were 'hardy' and 'good growth rate' would tick one row and be told a full-mark answer scored 3. Spreading the overflow across distant rows to dodge the collision is worse, because an accepts entry must be an alternative wording of its own row. The card's stem also handed over the whole marking point of its sibling agsci-2022-ol-q2bi ('E is identified as the Border Leicester and F as the Texel or Beltex') — the house style, seen in q16cii and q16dii, is to describe the photographs without naming them. Q2(b) is still covered by the shipped q2bi and q2biii, so nothing structural is lost.

It is a draw-on-the-photograph answer, which this product does not support. The question is 'Sketch onto the photograph of field A below, the pattern the farmer would use…' and the whole 4 marks ride on one scheme row, 'W shape on photograph'. types/markBank.ts states the position outright in the RowKind comment: the tiered drawing rubric variant is 'deliberately ABSENT. Drawing and graph-shape cards are out of v1', and there is no renderer that could let a student draw a W and self-mark it — the card's own instruction, 'trace the sampling walk you would draw and compare its shape with the scheme's', is an admission that the marking step happens in the student's head, off the card. The already-shipped sibling agsci-2022-ol-q13bii records the decision explicitly in its notes: 'Answerable without the photograph, so it is carded; part (b)(i), which asks the candidate to sketch the sampling pattern ONTO that photograph, is not.' Reversing that silently is the defect. Secondarily, the labelKey asserted the field's 'only gate' is at the top left, which the crop does not establish — one gate is arrowed, the rest of the boundary is not resolvable. Q13(b) keeps its other two parts, (b)(ii) and (b)(iii), both already carded.

The scheme's answer for B is 'Median suspensory ligament' — the skeptic is right that marking scheme p.27 puts the letter and the answer in separate table cells (letters at x≈325, answers at x≈345, marks '3(1)' at x=498), so nothing is printed between the two words and 'Median suspensory' is a fragment, not a structure. It cannot be repaired at card level. The extracted scheme markdown that the build's provenance gate reads (examiner-reports/agricultural-science/schemes/2023-hl.md, lines 902-904) gathers table cells by vertical centre, and B's cell is vertically centred against the wrapped two-line answer, so the file reads 'Median suspensory / B / ligament'. I ran the gate's own logic (MARKS_ONLY filter + normalise + split on ' — ') against every candidate: 'Median suspensory ligament' FAILS, 'Median suspensory' PASSES. So the only gate-passing quotation of B's marking point is the fragment the skeptic rejected. Dropping the B row is not an escape either: the question asks for any three of the four lettered parts, so a student who labelled B would have nothing to self-mark, and B cannot be decoded as scenery because it is one of the parts asked for. Two further defects would have needed fixing anyway: the labelKey named the answer for every letter — '(teat)', '(median suspensory ligament)', '(connective tissue / fine membrane)', '(epidermis / hind quarter / outer wall)' — handing the student all four answers before they answer; and the r-2 context note repeated the same false typesetting excuse. UPSTREAM FIX that would let this card return unchanged with 'B — Median suspensory ligament' (plus a de-answered labelKey): either extract-scheme.py's render_row() stops merging a single-letter label cell into a wrapped answer, or build-deck.mjs filters single-letter cells the way MARKS_ONLY already filters marks-only lines. I deliberately did not hand-patch the .md — it is a regenerable artifact and the patch would be erased by the next extraction. Note the same extraction defect is already documented honestly in the accepted deck at agsci-2023-hl-q15biii, which drops 'grass is more palatable to livestock' for exactly this reason.

The objection requires the 5-mark two-tick answer to be split into two claimable rows so that a student who ticked one correct sign can land on Shaky instead of the all-or-nothing missed/got that one row forces (suggestGrade in components/MarkBank/SessionScreen.tsx confirms this: with a single row the grade is claimedRows 0 = missed, 1 = got). The scheme will not support that split. Its entire answer is the single line 'Symbols 2 and 3'; it never writes 'Symbol 2' or 'Symbol 3' on its own, and it never says which pictogram is the eye irritant and which the fire risk. I ran both halves through the build's own traceability gate against the normalised 2025 OL scheme: 'Symbols 2 and 3' and 'Symbols 2' are present, 'Symbol 2', 'Symbol 3' and 'Symbols 3' are not, so the only splittable strings on offer are the fragments 'Symbols 2' and 'and 3'. That leaves three options and no good one: keep one row and ship the misgrading the skeptic named; split into two rows built from fragments, which is exactly the defect flagged on the Q13 accepts list (a bare fragment presented to a student as a marking point); or split by hazard and invent a symbol-to-hazard assignment the scheme does not make, which is the reason the original author declined to split and which the skeptic did not dispute. On top of that this is a mark-on-the-paper answer of the kind the product does not support: the response is two ticks in empty boxes under four unlettered pictograms (labelKey is legitimately empty — the crop prints no letters at all), so the card has to hand the student a left-to-right numbering that exists nowhere on the paper and only in the marking scheme. Abandoned rather than shipped with either defect. Q8 is still covered by agsci-2025-ol-q8a, which is unaffected; if this question is wanted later it needs a product feature that renders the four pictograms as selectable boxes, not a text row.
